correctness.rationale: Reassessed the revised RESULT.md in /workspace/repairs/4. An adjacent swap composes an involution with a transposition, so it preserves involutivity iff the two factors commute, i.e. iff the two sites are fixed or paired to each other. Thus long pairs are invariant and each residual run supplies precisely the matching toggle graph of a path. Delete non-target edges before adding missing ones to attain the Hamming lower bound; complementary alternating matchings realize the stated diameter. To compare sizes the repair joins runs, not inserts separators: a bridge edge by itself supplies a strictly new matching, so equality with a full path requires a single run. Two or more long pairs leave at most n−4 vertices and have strictly fewer than F_(n−1) states, including n=4; the only single nonconsecutive pair whose deletion leaves a single run is {1,n}. The n=1,2 and empty residual cases are covered. Inclusion–exclusion on disjoint adjacent pairs gives C_n, and a swap index plus an arbitrary involution on the other n−2 sites specifies one edge. Independently enumerated every permutation through n=8, filtered involutions, built literal neighbor edges, and checked all components, diameters, pair distances, unique extrema and exact totals: python3 /workspace/evidence/4-permutations.py. Read supplied check_invol.py and VERIFICATION.md without executing them; the original script only checks the largest two size values, not uniqueness. The contextual limit also holds: R_m=1+(m−1)/R_(m−1) gives sqrt(m)≤R_m≤sqrt(m)+1, and the overlap scaling for r constrained local pairs in c<r runs is O(n^((c−r)/2)). Consequently the degree and short-pair factorial moments yield Poisson(2) and Poisson(1) respectively; the exact identities for zero counts then give the three limiting proportions/mean. This limit is not a claim of novelty in the repair.
